target_customer: Glioblastoma patients, paid for via pharma partners and health systems if approved
problem: Glioblastoma has no effective standard salvage therapy; median survival after recurrence is 8 to 12 months.
business_model: Therapeutics developer; revenue only from drug sales or licensing after clinical success

founders.name: Andrew Bartynski
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC launch post as a repeat YC founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineered replicating retroviral vectors for in vivo tumor editing need preclinical efficacy, manufacturing and regulatory clearance for brain tumors.

defensibility.rationale: UCSF-derived platform (InViTE) with patent-based exclusivity and clinical regulatory barriers; unproven in humans.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; competitors run oncolytic herpes virus programs for glioblastoma, a different mechanism.

market_need_then: Recurrent glioblastoma has median survival of 8 to 12 months with no standard therapy (2022 review); company reports 90% survival in a mouse model, a company claim.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: cancer cells turned into biofactories minting their own destruction.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand coverage; recognition comes from science and the YC launch, not the name.

outcome_analysis: Kopra Bio is active, with preclinical data, a QB3 award and a reported $9.1M seed in June 2026 to test the therapy in humans. A Saudi hospital MoU signals partner interest. Outcome depends on clinical results, so success is still open and the record is capital-intensive biotech with long timelines.
notes: The UCSF page fetch was rate limited, so the $9.1M seed rests on search results citing UCSF Innovation and a FundUp date (2026-06-16); seed investors not found. QB3 award date not seen. Aggregators conflict ($125K, $500K, $600K, $9.7M totals). A report says the product is a non-lytic replicating retrovirus, so the oncolytic label is doubtful. Competitors found are 2024 to 2026 articles on other glioblastoma virus programs, not dated listings at founding, so the list is empty.
